role: The block callbacks World.setBlock runs besides storing a block: Block.onBlockAdded, Block.onNeighborBlockChange and Block.breakBlock for every class the native world reaches (liquids and the lava/water mix, falling blocks, fire and nether portal creation, torches, trapdoor, snow, cactus, ladder, vine, carpet, bed, cake, farmland, fence gate, doors, buttons, lever, bushes, reeds, the temple's tripwire, hooks, wire, repeater, comparator, dispenser facing, furnace facing, rails), plus the support-lost item drops through a pluggable environment.

structs.name: blockcb_env
structs.java: the World.rand stream, the Det roles and the EntityItem sink a callback's drop draws from; a global installed by the caller (explosion, structure half, activation, server tick)

structs.name: wire_changed
structs.java: BlockRedstoneWire.field_150179_b (the positions whose wire meta moved), fixed 256

gpu: its former globals, function statics and lazily built tables are gone (lane/gpuenv, L2): per-environment state lives in struct env (csrc/engine/env.h), per-dimension state in the replay's dims, constant tables are built before main; csrc/tests/globals.sh lists what is left
line 1376, file scope: struct blockcb_env blockcb_env is a global the callers overwrite and restore around their calls (global mutable state, function pointer item_drop plus void *ctx)
lines 1010-1011, file scope: static wire_changed[256] and wire_nchanged, BlockRedstoneWire's position set as global scratch

line 1420-1449, function drop_item_spawn: each drop goes through blockcb_env.item_drop or place_item_drop, which build an item entity in the caller (allocation site is the caller's, e.g. activate.c calloc)
is_class (line 98) compares class name strings from the registry at runtime

the callbacks are worklist steps (blockwl.h, lane/gpuworklist L7): a nested write, flag-1 metadata write, notification or immediate schedule is emitted and runs after the step; a callback whose body goes on after such a call is split into a step or a continuation op (the door, the rail reshape, the tripwire runs, the torch, trapdoor and bed tails, the liquids after the lava check); no recursion
function tripwire_hooks_step: one run direction per step, the walk bounded by pos < 42
function hook_update emits up to 55 ops in one step (a 40-wire line); BWL_EMIT_CAP is 128
notes: Redstone is switched off (world.conf): World's power queries answer 0 here, so wire strength, repeater and powered door, trapdoor and gate branches are dead; the tripwire and hook still rewrite meta for support and connectivity, as vanilla does during jungle temple generation. Pressure plates, signs, chests, flower pots and cocoa are named in comments of block_on_neighbor_changed; their bodies were not read line by line. The per-class Java member names are taken from this file's comments; func_150136_a for the hook update is inferred from BlockTripWireHook and not verified against the comment. Only test_itemuse.c includes blockcb.h directly; the other listed tests exercise it through world.c writes (not verified per test).
